Subject: ACME Bank — Region pinning & cross-region failover follow-up

Hi Laura / Rajesh —

Thanks again for taking time today — appreciate the deep dive on your data residency and failover requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

• Recap of asks from the call:
  - Primary requirement: All production inference + logs for EU customers must be stored and processed in EU regions (data residency).
  - Cross-region failover: You need automatic failover to a secondary region (US) if EU region becomes unavailable, but with controls to ensure PII processing is limited to EU where possible and failover is logged/audited.
  - Backups: Encrypted backups must be retained for 90 days with customer-side KMS option.
  - Logging: Audit logs accessible to Acme security team; retention and redaction controls required (PII redaction on logs).

• Proposed Redwood approach (high level):
  - Region pinning: Pin inference requests for EU customers to our EU fleet. We can enforce region by customer/route with policy rules.
  - Failover behavior: Synchronous primary-first routing with automated health checks. On primary failure we will route to the secondary (US). During failover we can optionally: 1) pause processing of requests flagged as PII-sensitive (recommended) or 2) allow failover with elevated audit logging (if you need availability over strict residency).
  - Backups: Encrypted snapshots of KV-cache and model artifacts to the customer-designated S3 with optional customer-managed KMS.
  - Logs & audit: Per-request logs stored in region of processing; we can redact user-provided text fields via regex rules before persisting. Full audit trail available via secure log export (s3/CloudWatch) per your preference.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll share a short design doc with details on routing rules, failover modes, and backup flows (attaching).
2) Marissa will follow up on SLAs for failover RTO/RPO and confirm any legal constraints for backups.
3) If this looks good, we can schedule a short technical review with your infra/security team next week.

Attaching the design doc & SOC2 summary for now.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao

Laura — great questions. Answers below and one operational recommendation.

1) PII during failover:
   - Default behavior: In failover mode we route requests to the secondary (US) only if you enable "failover-allow-pii". If disabled, requests flagged as PII-sensitive will return a 503 during failover (recommended for strict residency).
   - If you enable the flag for availability, we will restrict temporary writes: transient processing may occur in US memory/KV cache but persistent storage (logs, backups) will not be written to US unless explicitly permitted. All such events are flagged in the audit trail.

2) Log redaction and schema:
   - Redaction: Server-side, prior to persisting or exporting logs. We support field-level redaction based on keys and regex-based content filters.
   - Audit schema (summary): timestamp, request_id, route, model_version, region_of_processing, user_id_hash, pii_flag (true/false), action (serve/failover), error_code (if any). Full schema catalog attached in design doc.

3) Customer-managed KMS:
   - Yes — you can provide an AWS KMS key in your account. Redwood will.encrypt backups with that key; backups stored in the EU S3 bucket you provision. We can also support Bring-Your-Own-Cloud (BYOC) storage for extra isolation.

Operational recommendation: For your risk profile I recommend setting failover to "pause PII" by default and enable a manual override for the ops team when you need availability. This gives predictable residency guarantees while preserving the option for emergency failover.

I’ve attached a slightly updated design doc with the audit schema and the suggested failover modes. Marissa — can you confirm the SLA numbers we discussed (RTO <= 5 min for non-PII traffic, RTO <= 30 min for PII-pause mode) and whether Redwood’s canary failover meets Acme’s compliance review?

Thanks,
Aditya

Attachments: redwood-region-pinning-design.pdf (v2), SOC2-summary.pdf

Hi all — adding SLA/operational notes from our side: 

• SLA & RTO/RPO:
  - Non-PII traffic: target RTO = 5 minutes (automated routing + warm standby).
  - PII-pause mode: target RTO = 30 minutes (manual ops approval for temporary residency relaxation).
  - RPO for backups: configurable; default 24-hour snapshot, we can tighten to hourly if you require.

• Canary failover: We perform progressive routing shifts (canary) to limit blast radius; metrics and traces visible in Redwood Console for each step.

• Audit & evidence for compliance: We can provide per-incident export (zip) with request-level logs + internal incident timeline. SOC2-summary attached.

If this aligns, we can schedule the infra/security review — suggest Wed 09 Mar 2027 at 10:00 AM CET / 01:00 AM PT (open to adjusting).

Best,
